patch_description: The recommendation is exactly right: single-coordinate moves cannot fix the ratio because improving it usually requires moving the two closest points apart along their separating direction (both must move) and pulling the two farthest points inward. I add a dedicated `_pair_hillclimb` polisher that, at each step, identifies the pair realizing dmin and pushes both points apart along their connecting direction, and identifies the pair realizing dmax and pulls both inward, trying several step sizes and greedily accepting any move that improves (dmin/dmax)^2. It repeats until no improvement. This is cheap (14 points, O(1) pairs per step) and directly targets the only two distances that matter to the objective. It is inserted after the SLSQP polish and inside the perturbation loop.
